title: Multiply Strings
description:
Given two non-negative integers `num1` and `num2` represented as strings, return the product of `num1` and `num2`, also represented as a string.

You must implement the multiplication directly on the digit strings without using any built-in arbitrary-precision integer type (such as `BigInteger`) or converting the entire inputs directly to integers.

The returned string must not have any leading zeros unless the product itself is `"0"`.
constraints: num1 and num2 consist of digits only ('0'-'9').
Both num1 and num2 do not contain any leading zero, except the number "0" itself.
hints: The product of an m-digit number and an n-digit number has at most m + n digits.
Multiply each digit num1[i] by each digit num2[j]: their product contributes to positions i + j (carry) and i + j + 1 (ones place) in a result array of length m + n.
Remember to handle zero inputs cleanly and strip any leading zeros from the final digit array.

examples.explanation: Any number multiplied by "0" produces "0" with no leading zeros.
